items.stem: An employee wants to summarise a confidential contract using a free public AI tool. What is the main concern?

options.text: Confidential data may be stored or reused outside the organisation's control
options.rationale: Correct: pasting sensitive data into an unapproved tool risks exposure.

options.text: The summary will be too short
options.rationale: Length is not the key risk here.

options.text: There is no risk with contracts

options.rationale: The concern is data handling, not capability.

items.explanation: Correct: pasting sensitive data into an unapproved tool risks exposure.

items.stem: Which TWO habits make AI help at work more reliable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Read and fact-check AI output before sending it
options.rationale: Correct: review catches errors and fabrications.

options.text: Verify any specific facts or figures AI provides
options.rationale: Correct: AI can invent plausible but wrong details.

options.text: Forward AI drafts without reading them
options.rationale: Unread drafts can contain errors or wrong tone.

items.explanation: Correct: review catches errors and fabrications.

items.stem: A worker gets a vague AI answer to 'write a reply'. What most improves the result?

options.text: Adding context, audience, tone and the key points to include
options.rationale: Correct: specific context and constraints guide better output.

options.text: Repeating the same vague prompt louder
options.rationale: Repetition without detail does not help.

options.text: Removing all context to keep it short
options.rationale: Less context usually gives a weaker result.

options.text: Asking the AI to guess what is needed
options.rationale: Guessing yields generic, less useful output.

items.explanation: Correct: specific context and constraints guide better output.
